counterexample: At any month-end during roughly the first 3.9 years after .RP_START_DATE=2000-01-01 (t < .N_MIN_JUMP=200 weekly observations, engine.R:470 `if (t >= .N_MIN_JUMP)`), the paper's design would already have a full backtest running - section 4.3 holds (pi, mu~, Sigma~) fixed 'once and for all' from the full-sample Table 9 estimate before the out-of-sample loop even starts, so every rebalancing date from month 1 gets an ERC allocation. The engine instead emits NO portfolio row for any month-end before week 200 (engine.R:474 `if (is.null(.jp) ...) next`), and even after that point the allocation at month t uses mu~/Sigma~ re-estimated on the expanding window ending at t (engine.R:470-473, .sk_jump_params on .YM[seq_len(t),]) rather than the paper's single full-sample value - so the same calendar month can receive a different (mu~, Sigma~) under the engine's monthly refresh cadence than it would under the paper's one-time-for-the-whole-backtest parametrization, even though Sigma_t (the one object section 4.3 says should move) is estimated identically by the A.9 filter in both.
evidence: Section 4.3 ('Dynamics of out-of-sample ERC portfolios'): 'In the case of the ERC portfolio, it is common to consider a monthly rebalancing based on a one-year rolling covariance matrix' (rebalancing cadence + window length) and 'we assume that the parameters pi, mu~ and Sigma~ are given once and for all, and are set to the previous estimates. At each rebalancing date, we have to estimate the covariance matrix Sigma_t for the normal regime' (only Sigma_t moves; mu~/Sigma~ are static for the whole backtest). Table 9 caption: 'Estimation of the constrained mixture model when pi=0.5% (weekly model)'; confirmed (via live fetch of arxiv.org/html/2202.10721v1) that Table 10 ('Weights of the ERC portfolio') and Table 11 ('Volatility and skewness risks of risk-based portfolios') are both introduced immediately after and explicitly labelled as using this same weekly (pi=0.5%, Table 9) model with the monthly-rebalancing / one-year-rolling-window protocol of section 4.3 - i.e. the (weekly-estimation, monthly-rebalancing, 52-week window) cell the engine implements (.N_WIN_NORMAL=52L, .PI_JUMP=0.005, one month-end signal per calendar month) is the actual cell behind the paper's reported out-of-sample backtest, not an arbitrary pick among Table 9 vs Table 21 (monthly, pi=1.0%, used only as a footnote robustness check).
